title: Depthwise Convolution
text:
Depthwise Convolution
Key idea
• Apply one spatial filter to each input channel.
• No mixing between different channels.
• Output has the same number of channels as the input.
Mathematical form
For each channel c:
Yc = Xc ⋆Wc + bc
Takeaway
Depthwise Conv performs spatial filtering independently for each channel.

title: Depthwise Conv: Parameter Count
text:
Depthwise Conv: Parameter Count
General formula
Each input channel has one k × k filter:
#weights = Cin × k × k
If bias is used:
#biases = Cin
Total:
#parameters = Cin × k × k + Cin
Takeaway
Depthwise Conv has far fewer parameters than standard Conv2D because it
does not mix channels.

Depthwise Conv: Receptive Field
Single layer
For:
DepthwiseConv(k = 3, stride = 1)
each output value depends on:
3 × 3
input values from the same channel.
Important note
• Receptive field size is determined by kernel size and stride.
• Depthwise Conv does not combine information across channels.
Takeaway
Depthwise Conv has the same spatial receptive field as a standard Conv2D
with the same kernel size

title: Depthwise Separable Conv in PyTorch
text:
Depthwise Separable Conv in PyTorch
Implementation
import
torch.nn as nn
layer = nn.Sequential(
nn.Conv2d(
in_channels =32,
out_channels =32,
kernel_size =3,
padding =1,
groups =32
),
nn.Conv2d(
in_channels =32,
out_channels =64,
kernel_size =1
)
)
Explanation
• First Conv2d:
in channels=out channels= 32 and
groups=32 ⇒one 3 × 3 filter per
input channel (depthwise), no mixing
across channels yet.
• Second Conv2d: 1 × 1 with
in channels=32, out channels=64
⇒pointwise mixing from 32 to 64
channels.
• Together: spatial filtering (depthwise)
then channel mixing (pointwise) =
one depthwise-separable block.
• API: set groups=in channels to get
depthwise (here 32).

tensorflow as tf

tf.keras.layers.
DepthwiseConv2D (

),

# e.g. (B,H,W ,32) -> (B,H,W
32)

depth multiplier=1 ⇒same depth
as input.
• Conv2D 1 × 1: pointwise, filters=64.
• When: you want explicit depthwise
vs. pointwise layers (clear names /
weights).

tensorflow as tf

tf.keras.layers.
SeparableConv2D (

kernel_size =3,
padding="same",
depth_multiplier =1,
),
])
# (B,H,W ,32) -> (B,H,W ,64);
depthwise+pointwise
inside
Explanation
• Fuses depthwise + pointwise in one
layer; filters is the output channel
size after both steps.
• depth multiplier=1: one depthwise
filter per input channel (same spirit as
DepthwiseConv2D with multiplier 1).
• When: compact API; designs in the
Xception / MobileNet family.
